Measured identical on `9bf97ca`, `34df15d` and the binary that fixed the lift, so none of the carrier slices caused it. **Its neighbours do NOT raise**: `LIKE '%café%'`, `STARTING WITH 'café'` and `= 'café'` all answer 0 on the engine under the same attachment, so the rule is specific to the wildcard-FREE form. This server has no raise path under a real attachment at all - [carrier_expr_like] and [param_or_typed_term]'s LIKE guard are both gated on a byte-carrier ATTACHMENT - which is why it answers instead of raising. Held by two `eng_raises` cells in `serve-real-nonecmp` that go red if either server changes behaviour.~~ **DONE 2026-09-18** (`qa/serve-real-nonecmp.sh` 113 -> 138, 6 flip on `ae84769`) — implemented as [like_truncation_raise], a statement-level [PREPARE_REFUSAL] rather than a per-row `Term`, because the raise is **not value-gated**: it fires over an EMPTY table, over a row whose value is NULL, and under `1 = 0 AND`, and its two counts never move (`expected length 0, actual 1`) across pattern lengths and across VARCHAR(5), VARCHAR(20) and CHAR(8) alike. TWO call sites, because a COLUMN reaches [param_or_typed_term] carrying a Descriptor while an EXPRESSION reaches [resolve_expr_term]: `U || '' LIKE 'café'` and `UPPER(U) LIKE 'CAFÉ'` raise as well, and a fix to one leaves the other answering 0. The vector matches the engine's text word for word, both numbers included - which `agree` could never have held, since `sig()` collapses every failure to the single word REFUSE, so the cells use a new `both_raise` helper that fails if either side stops raising OR the texts diverge. **AND THE FIRST VERSION OF IT WAS A WRONG ANSWER.** With no blob guard, `B LIKE 'café'` REFUSED a statement the engine answers 0. Measured afterwards rather than assumed: the engine raises for a plain VARCHAR operand and stays quiet on SIXTEEN blob-typed shapes, while the broken binary raised on TWELVE of them - `B`, `UPPER(B)`, `LOWER(B)`, `TRIM(B)`, both concat directions, `COALESCE`, `CASE`, `IIF`, `SUBSTRING` and the mixed `U||B`/`B||U`. Excluded at the call site with [blob_result] - the predicate CONTAINING already uses - which walks Concat/Iif/Coalesce/Case and every text-answering function and so covers all twelve without naming one of them. **A gate cell added on a hunch caught it; neither probe matrix did**: the 60-cell shape matrix and the 30-cell boundary sweep both read 0 DIFF while that regression was live, because neither contained a blob.

### I. Stragglers in W1 / R / W7

Compound DESCENDING indexes scan; `fk_partner_has` with a text key
scans; a temporal/double scalar fold arrives as `Tok::FnExpr` and the
outer scans; the WHERE tokeniser cannot spell `-(9223372036854775808)`;
a statement `opt` cannot parse (`HAVING`) scans; `index_itype` stamps
`idx_string` regardless of charset (metadata divergence, no wrong
answer); RIGHT/FULL decline the inner index probe and the hash; probed
join sides must be plain tables; only an ORDER BY still materialises a
join; the `records_for` probe path rebuilds `page_sequence_map` per
outer row. W7: the triggers a statement gathers and the per-statement
clone of the cached check predicates (~127 µs) sit outside the cache.

## The growth chunk: the file grows the engine's way (done)

Laws pinned from `pag.cpp:430-700` (`PAG_allocate_pages`),
`tra.cpp:566-615` (`TRA_extend_tip`, called from `TRA_start` when
`number % transPerTIP == 0`), `dpm.epp:3146` (`extend_relation`) and
`DPM_pages`, then measured on live files:

1. **Pointer-page chain** (`ods::dml::extend_relation`). A full last
   pointer page chains a new one: `ppg_sequence` + 1, `ppg_eof` MOVED,
   `ppg_next` linked, `dpg_sequence = pp_sequence · dp_per_pp + slot`,
   and an `RDB$PAGES (relation, pag_pointer, sequence, page)` row for
   every relation but `RDB$PAGES` itself — the row `DPM_scan_pages`
   needs, without which the engine never reads the second page. The
   FIRST pointer page never uses its last slot (dpm.epp:3195 —
   `ppg_count < dp_per_pp - 1` for sequence 0).
2. **PIP chain + SCN pages** (`ods::dml::allocate_page`). PIP *n* lives
   at `n·pagesPerPIP − 1`, minted all-free when the previous PIP hands
   out its last bit; every multiple of `pagesPerSCN` (= `pagesPerPIP /
   32` = 2,041 at 8K, ods.cpp:63) is formatted as an SCN page and
   stepped over. `pip_used` is a HIGH-WATER mark (`PAG_last_page` sizes
   the file by it; `PAG_release_page` never lowers it — fc used to
   decrement it), `pip_min` = last bit + 1, `pip_extent` lowered on a
   release that frees a whole extent byte. `stamp_page_scns` stamps
   each page's era on the SCN page that OWNS it, slot `page %
   pagesPerSCN`, and an SCN page's own slot 0 carries its own era.
3. **TIP chain** (`ods::dml::ensure_tip_for`). The first id of a TIP's
   range mints it: zeroed page, prior `tip_next` linked, `RDB$PAGES (0,
   pag_transactions, sequence, page)` — a fresh engine database carries
   `(0, 287, 0, 3)` for TIP 0, so the row is the engine's own.

**Measured on the way.** `pip_used` on an engine file is NOT the
allocation mark either — `ensureDiskSpace` raises it to the size the
engine pre-extended the file to (a 64,000-row fixture read 65,312 with
1,300 bits still free); the gate sizes the PIP cell off the free bits.
The engine allocates data pages in aligned 8-page EXTENTS once a
pointer page holds 8; fc allocates one page at a time — same rows,
different page numbers, both readers indifferent (recorded, not
gated). A `SAVEPOINT` burns no id. And a silent no-op fell out of the
probing: `DECLARE I INTEGER = 0;` dropped its initialiser, so a `WHILE
(I < N)` body ran ZERO times and reported success — fixed
(`declared_var_inits`, initialisers run as the assignments they are;
one this server cannot read refuses the body).

**Residual, recorded:** `tip_chain_pages`, `extend_relation` and
`relation_data_pages` find their pages by scanning every page's type
byte — O(pages) per write, ~6 ms per INSERT on a 65k-page image. The
engine keeps these in `RDB$PAGES`-fed vectors; a per-database cache of
pointer-page and TIP page numbers is the next step when it dominates.

## Next, in order

- **SAME-POSITION TRIGGERS FIRE IN CREATION ORDER, NOT BY NAME DONE (2026-09-08, `serve-real-trigorder`):** fire-crab collected a table's triggers in creation (storage) order then re-sorted them by `(position, NAME)`, forcing an alphabetical tiebreak the engine does not use. A BEFORE trigger runs per row, so the order sets the final NEW value: three `BEFORE INSERT` at position 0 created `za_t`/`mb_t`/`ac_t` (appending Z/M/A) stored `ZMA` on the engine (creation order) and `AMZ` under the name sort - a silent wrong value. Dropped the `.then_with(name)` tiebreak at all three trigger-enumeration sites (`db_triggers` 15657, `ddl_triggers` 15799, `user_triggers` 16647); the collection is already creation-ordered and `sort_by` is stable, so equal positions keep creation order. Distinct positions were and remain correct (position dominates). The engine's same-position order is formally unspecified (an unstable sort over equal `RDB$TRIGGER_SEQUENCE`), but for triggers created in sequence it is creation order, which this matches; the fix is to STOP imposing a wrong deterministic order, not to reproduce the engine's instability.

- **A TRIGGER OR PROCEDURE BODY RUNS A CONSTRUCT THE ARITHMETIC BODY-GRAMMAR CANNOT HOLD DONE (2026-09-08, `serve-real-psqlbody`):** three gaps that made a runnable body refuse or mis-answer, all closed on the FIRE (interpret) path, which is the path a restore and `empbuild` use. (1) An EMPTY body (`begin end`) parsed to zero statements and `parse_trig_block` rejected the whole block, so ANY DML on a table carrying an empty trigger failed; an empty body is now a valid no-op, as the engine treats it. (2) An assignment whose right side is a CONDITIONAL (`COALESCE`/`CASE`) - which the arithmetic `fire_crab_ods::expr::Expr` grammar cannot represent - made the body refuse; the `TrigStmt::Assign` now carries an optional `raw: (text, binds)` kept as written, evaluated at fire time through the query planner (new `eval_raw_scalar`, mirroring `eval_raw_cond`: substitute `:var` and `NEW./OLD.` refs, `SELECT <expr> FROM RDB$DATABASE`, pull one row). Because a raw assignment needs the db, `trig_body_pure` now reports it non-pure so it takes the inline-with-db path. (3) A procedure statement reading a SCALAR SUBQUERY after its own INSERT (a running `SUM`) or over a system table (`COUNT` of `RDB$RELATIONS`) is evaluated the same way. A conditional body created THROUGH fire-crab is STILL refused at CREATE (`body_has_uninterpretable_blr` is true when `raw` is set - fire-crab will not emit BLR it cannot round-trip); the gate builds such triggers on the engine, the restore path. Found while gating trigorder.

- **TEMPORAL SUBTRACTION IS TYPE-DISCIPLINED, AND A TIMESTAMP DIFFERENCE ROUNDS DONE (2026-09-08, `serve-real-tempdiff`):** two silent wrong answers on date/time arithmetic, both from a third eight-surface differential hunt and pinned against FB6. (1) The engine allows a temporal difference only WITHIN a family (`add_datettime`): `DATE - DATE` (integer days), `TIME - TIME` (scale 4), `TIMESTAMP - TIMESTAMP` (scale 9, the `WITH TIME ZONE` spelling mixing freely with the plain one on the UTC instant). Every MIXED pair - a DATE against a TIMESTAMP either order and zoned or not, a TIME against anything but a TIME - is the engine's *expression evaluation not supported / -Invalid data type in DATE/TIME/TIMESTAMP addition or subtraction in add_datettime()* (42000). fire-crab's `Expr::type_of` for a temporal `Sub` had a catch-all `_ => Numeric` that INVENTED a fractional-day number for a DATE-vs-TIMESTAMP difference (`DATE - TIMESTAMP` answered `-0.416...`); the arm now types only the same-family pairs and refuses the rest at prepare, with `temporal_diff_shape` tightened to agree (the rank/width cascade must not contradict the type) and the eval arm carrying a fail-closed guard. (2) The scale-9 `TIMESTAMP - TIMESTAMP` value was computed by a TRUNCATING divide to nanodays where the engine rounds HALF AWAY FROM ZERO - a 10-hour difference is `0.416666667`, not the `...666` truncation gave (a stale note here had even called it truncation, from a case where the two coincide). TIME differences (exact) and `temporal + number` shifts were and stay correct; `temporal + temporal` was already refused.

- **NONE/OCTETS TEXT MEETING A REAL CHARSET: A CAST CARRIES THE RAW BYTES, AND AN EQUALITY/ORDERING COMPARISON WORKS IN BYTE SPACE DONE (2026-09-08, `serve-real-castnone` + `serve-real-nonecmp`):** the third hunt's top find, a silent wrong answer that DROPPED ROWS. isql's default attachment is effectively NONE, so a text literal arrives one char per octet (`'café'` is five carrier octets). Settled by a research workflow (6 differential slices + a code map) and then VERIFIED directly, including the crux the workflow argued: `WHERE u = _NONE x'FF'` is 0 rows with NO error while `CAST(_NONE x'FF' AS UTF8)` RAISES 22000 - so a comparison byte-compares and never validates, a CAST validates; two distinct models. **Stage A (`castnone`):** an unqualified `CAST(x AS VARCHAR(n))` takes the ATTACHMENT charset (measured: charset 4 under a UTF8 attachment, 0 under NONE); under a byte-carrier attachment the value moves into it via the engine's CVT_move ([transcode_text]) so the source's stored bytes pass through - `CAST(<utf8 'café'> AS VARCHAR(20))` is 5 octets / `char_length` 5, where fire-crab's carrier encoder had dropped é to one byte (4). The synthetic pad-wrap cast is excluded (its charset is the branches'); a real attachment is untouched. **Stage B (`nonecmp`):** a real-charset column compared to a byte-carrier literal now reinterprets the literal's octets in the column's charset ONCE at prepare (`adopt_carrier_literal` -> [transcode_text] from the byte-carrier attachment to the column set), turning it into a real-vs-real compare the existing machinery runs for `=`, `<>`, `<`, `>`, `<=`, `>=`, BETWEEN and IN; bytes that do not spell the set stay a carrier string that equals no real value - the engine's no-match / no-raise. `WHERE u = 'café'` over a UTF8 column now returns the row (was 0). No regressions: the 359-cell `textcolcmp`, `collate`, `index`, `join`, `orderby`/`groupby`/`distinct` and the cast/charset families all stay green, because the comparison change fires ONLY when one side is a byte carrier and the other a real charset, leaving same-charset and real-vs-real paths verbatim. **Recorded, NOT done (each its own path / measured contract):** LIKE / STARTING / SIMILAR / CONTAINING of a real column with a byte-carrier pattern (the engine's per-operator semantics differ - `<utf8> LIKE '<accented>%'` under NONE RAISES 22000, it does not answer); a hex-literal (`x'..'`, the `Rhs::Oct` expression path) equal to a real column's bytes; a text-BLOB column compared to a carrier literal (the `BlobText` expression path); a NONE/OCTETS COLUMN compared to a carrier literal (fc still returns 0 where the engine matches); column-vs-column cross-charset; the `_UTF8'..'` charset introducers (still cleanly REFUSED); and Stage D, teaching the index band to probe a real key from a reinterpreted carrier literal (a PLAN-only cosmetic today, rows already correct via scan).

- **CROSS-CHARSET COMPARISON EXTENDED TO THE EXPRESSION-PATH SHAPES DONE (2026-09-08, `serve-real-xcharcmp`):** the byte-space model, previously only on the literal fast path, now covers every operand shape that reaches the EXPRESSION comparison path - closing more dropped-row silent wrong answers. Settled by a research workflow (5 differential slices + a code map), verified directly incl. the crux that a comparison NEVER raises (`u = x'..FF'` is 0 rows, no error) where the same bytes through a CAST raise. **(1) NONE-column double-lift:** `param_or_typed_term` re-applied `to_carrier` to a literal a byte-carrier attachment had ALREADY delivered as a carrier string, so `n = 'café'` over a NONE column answered 0; the lift is now for a real-attachment literal only. **(2)** a new `Expr::CarrierEnc(inner, cs)` re-spells a REAL text value as the carrier of its OWN charset bytes (café -> its five UTF-8 octets); a byte carrier already is such a string. **(3)** `cmp_sides` (Text,Text) gained a byte-space block BEFORE the octets/collation branches: when EXACTLY ONE operand is a byte carrier and the other a real charset, wrap the real side in `CarrierEnc` and compare octets (through `OctKey` when OCTETS is involved, 0x00 pad; else `value_cmp`, 0x20 pad) - fixing a text BLOB vs a literal/column (`b='café'`), a hex literal (`u = x'636166C3A9'` matches; bad bytes 0/no-raise; reversed too), an OCTETS column vs a real literal, and column-vs-column (`u=o`, `u=n`, `u=b`). Two real charsets or two byte carriers fall through untouched, so the 359-cell `textcolcmp`, `collate`, `octets`, `index`, `join`, `orderby`/`groupby`/`distinct` all stay green. **(4)** `adopt_carrier_literal` now also reinterprets the pattern for STARTING WITH / CONTAINING / SIMILAR TO of a real text COLUMN, which the engine ANSWERS. **Recorded, NOT done:** LIKE with a carrier pattern (the engine SPLITS - `<utf8> LIKE '<accented>%'` RAISES 22000 while `LIKE '%<accented>%'` and exact `LIKE '<accented>'` ANSWER, a predicate that also turns on the column byte width); the BLOB pattern operators (`b CONTAINING '<accented>'`, a distinct pattern path); cross-charset JOIN key + mixed-carrier UNION (hashing/set-type, the riskiest); a text BLOB compared to a NUMBER (engine answers empty, fc still raises 22018); and the `_UTF8'..'` introducers (still refused). The wire 345 tests and every text/compare/index/join gate stay green.

- **A COMPUTED COLUMN TAKES ITS DECLARED FIELD TYPE, NOT THE EXPRESSION'S DONE (2026-09-08, `serve-real-computedtype`):** the fourth hunt's top find - one root cause behind three silent wrong answers. The engine wraps a `COMPUTED BY` expression in a CAST to the column's `RDB$RELATION_FIELDS` descriptor (blr_cast to the field format), so the value is ROUNDED to the column's scale, RANGE-CHECKED against its width, and DESCRIBED by its own wire type. fire-crab typed and evaluated the raw expression, so `INTEGER COMPUTED BY (ID/3.0)` answered `6.6` as INT64 scale -1 (should be `7`, LONG scale 0); `SMALLINT COMPUTED BY (ID*1000)` returned `100000` with NO error (should raise 22003); and `DOUBLE PRECISION COMPUTED BY (ID/3.0)` described as INT64, corrupting a prepared client's binding. The projection now injects `Expr::Cast(<resolved expr>, <declared target>)` and describes by the declared descriptor (`computed_cast_target` maps the field's dtype/scale/sub_type to an Int / Numeric / Approx cast; text/temporal/blob/DECFLOAT/FLOAT computed columns fall back to the expression's form, recorded). A neighbouring accuracy bug surfaced by the DOUBLE case is also fixed: the scaled->double conversion in the CAST, UNION and approx-arithmetic paths now DIVIDES by the power of ten (`exact_to_f64`, mirroring `CVT_get_double`) instead of multiplying by its reciprocal, so `20/3.0` as a DOUBLE is `6.600000000000000` to the last bit, not `...001`. **Recorded, NOT done:** a computed column used in a WHERE predicate or inside an expression (`WHERE c_int=7`, `id||c_int`) still REFUSES (42000) - the predicate/expression resolvers decline a computed field id; extending them to expand it to the same cast expression is a broader, separate chunk. No regressions: the wire 345 + ods 161 unit tests and the computed/double/union/numeric/cast/aggregate/index/join gates stay green.

- **A CAST OF AN OUT-OF-RANGE VALUE TO AN INT128-BACKED NUMERIC RAISES, AND AN IN-RANGE ONE KEEPS CLEAN DIGITS DONE (2026-09-08, `serve-real-int128cast`):** two silent wrong answers on the approximate-source cast to a NUMERIC/DECIMAL of precision 19..38 (an INT128 backing), from the fourth hunt and a numeric-typing research pass. The overflow bound is the BACKING INT128 range (`|scaled| <= 2^127-1`), independent of the declared precision. fire-crab (1) SATURATED to 2^127-1 instead of raising 22003 - `CAST(1e39 AS NUMERIC(38,0))` answered `170141183460469231731687303715884105727` where the engine raises numeric-value-out-of-range; and (2) stored the double's EXACT BINARY expansion for an in-range value - `CAST(1.5e38 AS NUMERIC(38,0))` came back `150000000000000006067947700923341471744`. The `CastTarget::Numeric` approximate branch now, for the 16-byte backing only, raises with the exact 2^127 gate the integer-target cast already uses, and converts the double through its SHORTEST round-trip decimal (its decimal significance) so `1.5e38` is `1.5x10^38` with clean low digits. The narrower backings (2/4/8) are untouched - a double large enough to reach them already overflows to 22003. **Recorded, NOT done:** the exponent-form literal typing (fire-crab types every `<sig>e<exp>` DOUBLE; the engine types a significand past i64 as an EXACT type, but the INT128-vs-DECFLOAT(34) boundary needs more measurement - `9223372036854775808e0` is INT128 while `12345678901234567890e0` is DECFLOAT(34) despite fitting i128, so a naive "fits i128 -> INT128" rule is wrong); DECFLOAT precedence in COALESCE/CASE; and a double literal with >16 significant digits cast to a wide NUMERIC (the engine constant-folds the literal's extended decimal digits, beyond a double's precision). No regressions: the wire 345 tests and the castrange / cast / numeric / computed / double / union gates stay green.

- **EXPONENT-FORM NUMERIC LITERAL TYPING MATCHES THE ENGINE DONE (2026-09-09, `serve-real-explit`):** fire-crab typed EVERY `<mantissa>e<exp>` literal DOUBLE, so a high-significand one lost precision AND announced the wrong SQLDA type (`12345678901234567890e0` came back as a lossy `1.234567890123457e+19` DOUBLE where the engine keeps the exact `12345678901234567890` DECFLOAT(34)). Settled by a focused research workflow (dense boundary walk + downstream-safety audit + code map) and VERIFIED directly. The rule is by the SIGNIFICAND alone (mantissa digits, point removed, leading zeros dropped) as a magnitude M - NOT the net value or the exponent: `M <= 2^63-1` -> DOUBLE (so `1e40`, significand 1, stays DOUBLE); `M == 2^63` EXACTLY -> INT128 (a lone quirk - `9223372036854775808e0/e1/e5`, whole scale-0 only); `M >= 2^63+1` -> DECFLOAT(34) (`9999999999999999999e0`, `1.2345678901234567890e5`, a 40-digit significand). One shared `classify_exp_literal` feeds BOTH the SELECT lexer (`expr_atom_bare`) and the WHERE lexer (`numeric_tok`), so they cannot disagree; the DOUBLE branch parses the ORIGINAL text (byte-identical to before), INT128 reuses `RawExpr::Int128`/`Tok::Int128`, DECFLOAT(34) `text_to_dec128` + `RawExpr::DecFloat34`/`Tok::DecFloat34` (with `tok_lhs_raw` and `texpr_atom_bare` gaining the DecFloat34 arm). **Recorded, NOT done:** a DECFLOAT literal (exponent OR plain) in a WHERE COMPARISON, a CAST-to-another-type, or a concat still REFUSES 42000 - DECFLOAT is not yet a comparison/merge type (its own type-system chunk); this is the SAME limitation a plain large literal already has, gated here as a known-refuse rather than a wrong value. And a 2^63 significand that would need a SCALED or ROUNDED INT128 (`9223372036854775808e-1`, `9.223372036854775808e18`) is REFUSED (no Int128 literal carries a scale; the engine types it INT128). No regressions: the wire 345 tests and the literal / numeric / decfloat / cast / castrange / double / union / arith gates stay green.

- **UTF8 LOWER/UPPER USE THE ENGINE'S PER-CHARACTER SIMPLE CASE MAPPING DONE (2026-09-09, `serve-real-utf8case`):** a fourth-hunt HIGH that silently DROPPED ROWS. fire-crab cased a UTF8 string with Rust's `to_lowercase`/`to_uppercase` (the FULL, sometimes multi-char Unicode mapping) and kept a character UNCHANGED whenever that mapping was multi-char - right for `'ß'` UPPER and for a ligature, but WRONG for U+0130 LATIN CAPITAL LETTER I WITH DOT ABOVE: its full lowercase is `'i'` + COMBINING DOT ABOVE (two chars) while its SIMPLE lowercase - what the engine applies per character - is a single `'i'` (U+0069). So `LOWER('İ')` stayed `'İ'` (2 octets) where the engine answers `'i'` (1 octet), and `WHERE LOWER(nm)='istanbul'` silently dropped an `'İSTANBUL'` row. Fixed in `fire_crab_ods::intl::simple_case` by mapping U+0130 to `'i'` on lowercasing; every other casing edge already matched the engine (probed: `ß`, `ẞ`, the ligatures, dotless `ı`, `İ` under UPPER, the accented Latin-1 letters). No regressions: the wire 345 + ods 161 unit tests and the case / collate / collation / textcolcmp / charset gates stay green.

- **A CONDITIONAL WITH A DECFLOAT BRANCH NO LONGER RENDERS A CONFIDENT WRONG VALUE DONE (2026-09-09, `serve-real-dfcond`):** the DECFLOAT type-system's first, safe stage - closing the silent wrong answers that a research workflow (3 contract slices + type-system map) surfaced, without the full `ExprType::DecFloat` fan-out. fire-crab has no `ExprType` for DECFLOAT, so `conditional_type`'s fold DROPPED a DECFLOAT branch (its `type_of` is None) and COALESCE/CASE/IIF/DECODE took the SIBLING's type - `COALESCE(<decfloat>, <int>)` came back `0`, and `COALESCE(<int>, <decfloat>)` / `NULLIF(<decfloat>, <int>)` were latently wrong the same way (a NULL int, or a mismatched NULLIF, would render the decfloat truncated). The engine types such a mix DECFLOAT and coerces the other branch into it. Until fire-crab has a real DECFLOAT result type (the larger chunk), `conditional_type` now REFUSES a conditional that contains a DECFLOAT branch (`is_decfloat_arith`), and `type_of` REFUSES `NULLIF` with a DECFLOAT first operand rather than borrowing the second operand's type - a clean 42000 instead of a wrong value (match-or-refuse). A pure-decfloat conditional already refused; non-decfloat conditionals, and `NULLIF(<int>, <decfloat>)` (int first operand -> INTEGER), are unchanged. DECFLOAT COLUMN comparisons already work (via `decfloat_term`); a UNION with a DECFLOAT leg already refused. **Recorded, NOT done (the full DECFLOAT type-system):** a real DECFLOAT result type for a conditional (correct DECFLOAT value+SQLDA, not a refuse); a DECFLOAT LITERAL in `=`/`IN`/concat; `CAST` to/from DECFLOAT; DECFLOAT-vs-DOUBLE comparison (width-follows-the-decfloat-operand); SUM/AVG over DECFLOAT; and a decimal64 `round_to_dec16` top-exponent encoder bug (`1E+384` -> garbage; `>= 1E+385` should raise 22003). No regressions: the wire 345 unit tests and the condtext / decfloat / numeric / cast / union gates stay green.

- **A MERGE READS ITS STATEMENT-START SNAPSHOT, NOT ITS OWN WRITES DONE (2026-09-09, `serve-real-mergesnap`):** a fourth-hunt HIGH that CORRUPTED both the rowset and the persisted state - a Halloween problem. A MERGE is one request over one image: every subquery that reads the target (in a `WHEN MATCHED ... UPDATE SET`, a `WHEN MATCHED ... AND <cond>`, or a `WHEN NOT MATCHED ... INSERT VALUES`) evaluates against the target as it stood at statement start, exactly as a plain searched UPDATE does. fire-crab's `merge_exec` desugared each matched row into a per-row UPDATE run against the LIVE, growing image, so `WHEN MATCHED THEN UPDATE SET n = (SELECT SUM(n) FROM t)` grew `60,110,200` (each row reading rows written before it) where the engine writes `60,60,60`. Settled by a research workflow (MERGE + UPDATE-OR-INSERT stability slices + execution map) and verified directly. The fix arms the existing `SubqImageGuard` (the pre-statement-image override `Database::bytes` already honors for RETURNING) around ONLY the per-branch `plan_update`/`plan_delete`/`plan_insert` FOLD - where the SET/condition subqueries are evaluated and the correlated lookups built - and drops it before `execute_dml_collecting`, so the WRITE still lands on the live image and earlier rows' writes accumulate (a first draft that armed the guard over the whole write phase re-based every row off the frozen image and lost all but the last install - caught by direct measurement). A plain UPDATE / DELETE / UPDATE OR INSERT never enters `merge_exec` and is untouched (already stable). Verified: SUM/COUNT/MAX/`n+SUM`/correlated/`set from source`/`n=n+1` matched updates, a NOT MATCHED insert whose VALUES read the start-of-statement sum (both new rows 60), and the plain-UPDATE and delete-below-avg controls. No regressions: the wire 345 unit tests and the merge / mergeparam / returning / corrsub / insert / update / trigger / updateorinsert gates stay green.

- **LPAD / RPAD ENFORCE THE VARCHAR-RESULT BYTE LIMIT DONE (2026-09-09, `serve-real-padlimit`):** a fifth-hunt HIGH - a confident value with the wrong cardinality where the engine refuses. An LPAD/RPAD result is a VARCHAR whose declared byte width is the pad length N times the SOURCE charset's bytes-per-character; when that exceeds 65535 the engine raises 54000 *Implementation limit exceeded* AT PREPARE, even wrapped in `CHAR_LENGTH` (which otherwise consumes the string). fire-crab built the over-long string and answered a value - `CHAR_LENGTH(LPAD('Hi',16384,'*'))` returned 16384 under a UTF8 attachment where the engine errors, and announced an impossible VARYING width. The boundary is charset-exact (measured): a NONE/single-byte source caps at N=65535, UTF8 (4 bytes/char) at N=16383 (16383x4=65532 answers, 16384x4=65536 raises). Fixed at the LPAD/RPAD resolution: when a LITERAL length N makes `N x bytes_per_char(source charset) > 65535`, resolve refuses, so the refusal propagates through any enclosing expression. A non-literal length keeps the current fallback (the rare dynamic case). No regressions: the wire 345 unit tests and the string / textwidth / charform / cast gates stay green.

- **TWO SILENT-WRONG SUBQUERY/RECURSION SHAPES REFUSED DONE (2026-09-09, `serve-real-subqarity` + `serve-real-recorder`):** two fifth-hunt finds, settled by a research workflow (traversal-order + arity contract + executor map) and verified directly. **(1) Subquery arity:** a subquery used as a SCALAR operand, an IN/NOT IN right side, or a quantified (ANY/ALL/SOME) operand must project exactly ONE column - the engine raises 07002/-104 "count of column list and variable list do not match" at prepare, independent of cardinality. fire-crab folded the multi-column inner away and then took COLUMN 1, silently answering a WRONG ROWSET (`WHERE a = (SELECT x, x*10 FROM t2)` returned the a=1 row). Fixed at the single choke point `corr_describe` with a `scalar_arity` gate (refuse when the operand degree != 1); EXISTS is exempt (passes `scalar_arity=false`) and a single-column operand is unchanged. **(2) Recursive-CTE FIRST/SKIP without ORDER BY:** the engine walks a WITH RECURSIVE depth-first in RECORD-NUMBER (storage) order, fire-crab breadth-first (a level queue) - the SAME SET, a different ORDER - so a top-level `FIRST`/`SKIP`/`ROWS` slices a DIFFERENT SET OF ROWS (measured: `FIRST 3` of a tree walk is the engine's {1,1/2,1/2/4} vs fc's {1,1/2,1/3}). fire-crab has no record-number model and structurally cannot reproduce the engine's sibling order (a stack would trade one wrong order for another), so it now REFUSES a recursive CTE with FIRST/SKIP/ROWS and no top-level ORDER BY (which is exactly where the ROWSET, not just the order, diverges); a top-level ORDER BY makes the two byte-identical and stays open, and the unlimited walk (order-only, same set) and a linear numbers series are left answering. Both are refuse-not-wrong fixes; a DISTINCT (order-independent) and a partial-key ORDER BY are noted narrowings. No regressions: the wire 345 unit tests and the recursive / cte / corrsub / subquery / view gates stay green.

- **DECFLOAT(16) ENCODES A HIGH-EXPONENT VALUE CORRECTLY AND RAISES ON OVERFLOW DONE (2026-09-10, `serve-real-dec16emax`):** a recorded confident-wrong-value (garbage) from the DECFLOAT type-system research. A decimal64's stored exponent must be <= 369 (biased <= 767), but `encode_dec64` was handed a value with a higher exponent and a short coefficient - a cast of `1E+384` arrives as coefficient 1, exponent 384 - and the out-of-range `biased` overflowed the two combination-field exponent bits, garbling the whole word: `CAST('1E+384' AS DECFLOAT(16))` answered `8.000000000000001E-369` where the engine answers `1.000000000000000E+384`. And a magnitude past the format's range (adjusted exponent > emax 384, `1E+385`) must raise 22003 *Decimal float overflow*; fire-crab produced more garbage. `encode_dec64` now NORMALISES - it pads the coefficient with trailing zeros to bring the stored exponent down to 369 while it stays within 16 digits - and a new `fit_dec64` (round to 16 sig, normalise, then REFUSE what still will not fit) is routed from the DECFLOAT(16) cast (raising 22003) and the decimal64 store paths (`round_to_dec16_of`). Mid-range and small values are byte-identical. No regressions: the wire 345 + ods 161 unit tests and the decfloat / numeric / cast / int128cast / explit gates stay green.

- **UNARY MINUS OF A SMALLINT / INTEGER MINIMUM RAISES, IT DOES NOT WRAP DONE (2026-09-10, `serve-real-negoverflow`):** a sixth-hunt HIGH - a confident wrong scalar. Negation is `0 - x`; when `x` is the minimum of its type the positive result overflows the type width, so the engine raises 22003 *Integer overflow* (`-CAST(-2147483648 AS INTEGER)` is +2147483648, one past INT32_MAX). fire-crab computed +2147483648 correctly but announced the result in a 2/4-byte SMALLINT/INTEGER wire slot, so the client read a WRAPPED value back (`-32768` / `-2147483648`). The i64 (BIGINT) and i128 negations already carried their `checked_neg`; only the i16/i32 backing lacked a check. Added a narrow-integer range check at the projection choke point `ProjCol::value_of` - beside its existing "an INT128 value in a non-INT128 wire raises" guard - so an exact result whose backing integer leaves the announced SMALLINT/INTEGER range raises 22003 before the wire slot truncates it. It runs only for COMPUTED columns (a stored value always fits), and tests the BACKING integer so a `NUMERIC(p,0)` / `NUMERIC(p,s)` over the same width is covered too. (First draft added the check to the wrong `match` arm - the stored-column path - and was inert; caught by a trace.) No regressions: the wire 345 unit tests and the arith / numeric / cast / computedtype / index / join gates stay green.

- **AN ARRAY-ELEMENT SUBSCRIPT IN A WHERE FILTER READS THE REAL ELEMENT DONE (2026-09-10, `serve-real-wherearr`):** the sixth hunt's highest-blast-radius silent wrong - a wrong RESULT SET on any query filtering by an array element. Settled by a research workflow (contract slices + eval map) and verified directly. **Root cause (not the tokenizer, not an unarmed blob context):** `expr_reads` had no `Expr::ArrayElem` arm, so `project_read_len` under-estimated the natural-scan partial-decompression length and stopped BEFORE the array column (`JOB.LANGUAGE_REQ` is JOB's last field) - the slot stayed undecoded and every array-element read collapsed to NULL, in the WHERE filter (wrong COUNT: `WHERE coalesce(language_req[1],'x')='x'` was 31, engine 21) AND in the projection under a scan filter. It was access-path-dependent: a leading-equality predicate chose an index (whole record decoded -> correct) and a no-WHERE query decoded everything (`project_read_len` returns MAX), so only the natural-scan-with-filter path truncated. Fixed by adding the `ArrayElem` arm to `expr_reads` (mark the array `fid` and walk the subscripts); over-estimating the read length is always safe. **Second, independent fix:** a BARE `COL[i]` subscript in WHERE/HAVING/ON refused at prepare because the predicate tokenizer had no arm for `[` (only function-wrapped forms slipped through, which is how the NULL-read surfaced); a new `matching_bracket` + a tokenizer arm now lexes `COL[...]` whole through the char-expression parser, so a bare subscript reads the real element and matches the engine. **Recorded, still REFUSED (a separate slice, law-safe):** a subscript in HAVING over the grouped element and in a JOIN ON. No regressions: the wire 345 unit tests and the arrays / wherefn / wherexpr / numericwhere / textnumwhere / where / having / join / groupby gates stay green.

  - **A TEXT VALUE TOO LONG FOR ITS COLUMN RAISES THE ENGINE'S 22001** - on every write path, carrying the two counts the client needs: `string right truncation, expected length 5, actual 7`. fire-crab answered a bare Dynamic SQL Error (42000) for ALL of them. Two roots, one law: at EXECUTE, [encode_wire_value] returns a plain `None` when the value does not fit and each caller mapped that to its own generic message; at PLAN, a LITERAL fails in [encode_set_value], so `UPDATE T SET S = 'abcdefg'` was refused as a statement this server cannot plan - and a MERGE inherited that refusal through the UPDATE its branch desugars to. Measured on both sides, cell by cell: UPDATE and INSERT with a literal, a concatenation (actual 8), `INSERT .. SELECT`, MERGE, `UPDATE .. RETURNING` and a bound `?`, into VARCHAR and CHAR alike.
    `expected` is the column's declared CHARACTER count and `actual` the value's own **in the DESTINATION's characters** - one byte IS one character in a byte carrier, which is why five two-byte characters into a `VARCHAR(5) CHARACTER SET NONE` report 10 while seven of them into a `VARCHAR(5) UTF8` report 7. CHAR takes the same rule and its blank padding is NOT counted here (unlike the OUT-capacity rule, where a CHAR counts its padding); a value that fits still pads silently.
    The fix keeps ONE implementation of the fit rule, because a copy of it went stale once already: [text_bytes_for] now reports WHY it failed (`TextFit::TooLong` with the counts, or `Other`) instead of a bare `None`, the five execute paths ask [fit_or] and the two planners ask [set_value_fit_error] over the SAME wire value [encode_set_value] builds. A too-long literal becomes `Plan::RefusedEval(StringTruncation)` - a plan that RAISES rather than a statement that cannot be planned - which is what carries the vector into MERGE's per-row branches with no change there at all. A character with no image in the destination set stays the engine's OWN 22018 *Cannot transliterate character between character sets*, which is why the fit probe answers a reason rather than a bare refusal (`serve-real-textfit`, NEW gate, 2026-09-16).

So a MERGE doubled EVERY non-ASCII literal it carried, under EVERY attachment charset: a `SET` value (`SET V = 'éé'` stored 8 octets for the engine's 4), a literal in the SOURCE select, and - the sharpest - one in the `ON` or `WHEN .. AND` condition, where the doubled text simply stopped COMPARING EQUAL, so the row was silently not matched and the branch never fired at all. A hex literal and a column value were never affected, and the plain `UPDATE` twin of the same clause was always right: it never comes through here. It iterates characters now (`'` and `?` are ASCII, so the marker scan is unchanged).
    **What made it hard, and what fixed that:** nothing printed the desugared per-row statement, so four successive hypotheses (the constant fold, [stmt_text_decode], a carrier-specific path, [merge_subst]'s assembly) were each disproved only by measurement. `FC_SRV_TRACE` now prints each desugared branch statement WITH ITS BYTE LENGTH - a literal encoded once too often reads identically on a UTF-8 console and differs only in the count - and that one line located it immediately. Measured: `SELECT 'é' || u` (u UTF8) under a NONE attachment is `OL 7 / CL 5` on the engine and `OL 9 / CL 6` here; the cast forms follow 7 -> 9. A NONE column agrees, an ASCII literal agrees, and every shape agrees under a UTF8 attachment. It fails on the previous binary too, so it predates this slice; `serve-real-castnone` carries the agreeing NONE-column cell and records this one beside it.
    **THE CONTRACT, MEASURED IN FULL (2026-09-16) - and an attempt that was WITHDRAWN.** A 42-cell matrix (both operand orders x NONE / UTF8 / WIN1252 attachments x 2- and 3-byte characters x ASCII and non-ASCII column values x the store paths) plus `SET SQLDA_DISPLAY ON` for every shape pins the engine's rule:
    * the RESULT SET follows [cs_join] - OCTETS absorbs, a real set beats the attachment sentinel, NONE is weakest - and the describe then RE-ANNOUNCES it in the attachment's charset, except OCTETS which keeps its own (measured: under NONE `'é' || <utf8>` is charset 4, `'é' || <win1252>` 53, `'é' || <octets>` 1; under UTF8 everything is 4 but OCTETS stays 1; under WIN1252 everything is 53 but OCTETS stays 1);
    * the VALUE is each operand MOVED INTO THE JOIN SET (CVT_move), carrier <-> real being a raw byte copy: under a NONE attachment `'é' || <utf8 'ab'>` is 3 characters / 4 octets, the literal's two CARRIER chars read as the one UTF-8 character they spell;
    * and under a REAL attachment THE FIRST OPERAND DECIDES, which the asymmetry proves: under WIN1252 `'é' || <utf8>` is 4 octets / 4 chars while `<utf8> || 'é'` is 6 / 4, and under UTF8 `'é' || <win1252>` is 4 / 3 against `<win1252> || 'é'`'s 3 / 3 - same characters, different octets, because OCTET_LENGTH reads the JOIN set while both orders announce the same charset.
    fire-crab gets the value wrong wherever a LITERAL meets an operand of another set: the eval arm joins two `String`s with a bare `format!`, and a `String` means different things per charset here (a byte carrier's octets ride one char per byte, a real set's are characters).
    **The attempt - a width-transparent `Expr::CsMove` wrapper inserted per operand by a shared `concat_expr`, with the sentinel resolved before the join - fixed all 42 cells and was reverted anyway**, because it broke three things a narrower view had hidden. Any future fix has to satisfy ALL of these at once: (1) a BYTE-CARRIER result counts each operand's BYTES, so `<UTF8 VARCHAR(32)> || <OCTETS VARCHAR(32)>` must announce 160 and not 64 - measuring the operands in the JOINED set instead of their own is what produced 64 (`serve-real-concatcs`, 18 cells); (2) one BINARY operand makes the whole result binary, subtype 0, not subtype 1 UTF8 (`serve-real-blobexpr`); (3) a LITERAL must keep carrying BOTH of its widths until emission - resolving the sentinel inside [text_form] collapses a decision [resolve_text_cs] makes later, and the unit test `a_literal_carries_both_of_its_widths` pins exactly that; (4) a COLUMN || COLUMN pair must NOT be re-decoded - applying CVT_move to every operand changed bytes that were already right, which is what took `serve-real-concatcs` from 0 to 18 DIFFs while the literal-bearing probes stayed green. The lesson for the next attempt: the value probes only covered literal-bearing shapes, so they could not see a column-only regression; run `concatcs` and `blobexpr` on EVERY iteration, not at the end.

What nothing checked was the ROWS, and the gate's own header said why: it recorded that they "live in per-connection temporary space at runtime, which is not part of what fire-crab writes". They were part of what it wrote. Measured against the live engine: `ON COMMIT DELETE ROWS` kept its rows through the commit that should have emptied them (2 where the engine says 0) and through a ROLLBACK (2 vs 0), and a FRESH ATTACHMENT read the previous one's rows in both kinds (2 and 2 vs 0 and 0) - a silent wrong answer on a shape this server already accepted, which outranks the LOCAL TEMPORARY TABLE gap beside it, since that one at least refuses honestly.
    **The engine's contract, measured in full** (one attachment unless said): in-transaction 2; after COMMIT, DELETE ROWS 0 and PRESERVE ROWS 2; after ROLLBACK 0; **after COMMIT RETAIN 2, for BOTH kinds**; a fresh attachment 0 and 0. GTT rows also honour SAVEPOINTS (`rollback to savepoint` takes 3 rows to 2) and a rollback undoes a DELETE as well as an INSERT. Concurrently (two driver connections): each attachment sees only its own rows, A's commit leaves B's untouched, and **A's DETACH does not remove B's PRESERVE rows**.
    **THE FIRST DESIGN WAS THE WRONG ONE AND THE MEASUREMENT KILLED IT.** A per-connection in-memory row store looked obvious - `Database` is per connection, and `RowSource::TableScan` already has the [mon_rows] seam for rows that come from somewhere other than pages. But GTT rows honour rollback and savepoints, so that store would have had to re-implement the undo windows and MVCC the pages already provide correctly. **What was missing was never the storage; it was the two moments the rows are supposed to die.** So the rows stay on the pages and the fix is two purges: at every non-retaining COMMIT for type 5, riding the committing transaction so its delete stubs become real with it, and at DETACH for both types, under a committed id of its own (the attachment's transaction has just been killed, and nothing after it would flush).
    **The two guards are not decoration.** The commit purge runs UNGUARDED because `collect_dml_targets` sees only what this attachment sees - another attachment's uncommitted rows are invisible to it, so the MVCC that already hides them is what makes it safe. The DETACH purge runs ONLY WHEN THIS IS THE LAST ATTACHMENT, because the engine keeps a second attachment's PRESERVE rows across the first's detach and fire-crab holds every attachment's rows in one shared file where the purge cannot tell whose are whose: with somebody else attached it does nothing, leaving the old wrong answer (rows outstaying their attachment) rather than creating a new one (deleting a live session's data).
    **RECORDED, NOT FIXED, and NOT this slice's doing:** through ISQL a `COMMIT RETAIN` over a DELETE ROWS GTT leaves the engine 2 rows and fire-crab 0. The wire contract is not what differs - driven through firebird-driver every form agrees (`commit(retaining=True)` 2, a following plain commit 0, a plain commit after an insert 0, the DSQL text `COMMIT RETAIN` 2). What differs is that isql sends fire-crab an EXTRA plain `op_commit` (op 30) straight after the retaining statement, and that commit legitimately empties the table. The op sequence is byte-for-byte identical on the previous binary, so the purge only made it visible; what isql is answered about a DSQL COMMIT RETAIN is its own chunk. **CORRECTION, measured after that entry was written:** the trigger is NOT the ROLLBACK that happened to precede the retain in the first probe - it is ANY EARLIER TRANSACTION END IN THE SAME isql SESSION. Bisected, each a fresh session ending in `COMMIT RETAIN` then a count, engine 2 throughout: `INSERT; INSERT; COMMIT RETAIN` **agrees** (fc 2); `INSERT; COMMIT; INSERT; INSERT; COMMIT RETAIN` diverges (fc 0); the same with `ROLLBACK` in place of that COMMIT diverges; the full original diverges. So one prior commit is enough and the rollback was incidental. NOT the cause either: the statement TYPE, which is identical on both servers through the driver - `COMMIT` 10, `COMMIT RETAIN` 10, `ROLLBACK RETAIN` 11 - so isql is not dispatching on it. What IS measurably different is the size of the `op_response` chunks each server writes (the engine's 32 bytes against fire-crab's 24, seen through a relay), but that holds for every response in the session including the agreeing one, so it is a lead and not the cause. Settling it needs a relay that FRAMES the protocol rather than sampling chunk boundaries - the first step of that chunk. **AND THE SERVER'S OWN HANDLING IS NOT AT FAULT**, which narrows that chunk to one question. Replayed through firebird-driver with no isql anywhere, the diverging sequence AGREES: engine 2, fire-crab 2, and the ops fire-crab receives after the retaining statement are `63, 67, 62, 68` - **no op 30 among them**. isql sends that extra commit; the driver never does, and fire-crab answers every op it is actually sent correctly. What remains to find is what fire-crab REPLIES to the executed COMMIT RETAIN that makes isql follow up with a commit the engine is not sent.

    **A SURVIVOR LIMIT IS A THIRD ANSWER, not either half of the two already implemented.** A filter alone does not stop a body (five iterations) and a limit alone stops it at the nth SUSPENDED row; together they stop it at the nth row that PASSES. Measured against the live engine: `FIRST 1 WHERE K > 3` 4, `FIRST 1 WHERE K > 0` 1, `FIRST 2 WHERE K > 2` 4, `FIRST 3 WHERE K > 1` 4, `ROWS 2 WHERE K > 2` 4, `FIRST 1 SKIP 1 WHERE K > 1` 3 (so the bound is `skip + take` SURVIVORS, the same sum the unfiltered cap uses), and a filtered limit through a DERIVED TABLE 3.
    **THE CAP GREW A PREDICATE RATHER THAN THE WALKER GROWING A SPECIAL CASE.** `PsqlFrame::stop_after` becomes a `BodyCap { take, keep: Option<Predicate> }`, and the SUSPEND site asks *does the consumer keep this row?* BEFORE the push, counting the cap down only when it does - `keep: None` is the unfiltered limit and `EXECUTE PROCEDURE`'s own rule, both unchanged. The `Derived` arm of [materialise_procedures] therefore stops SWALLOWING a cap when a filter is present and instead binds that filter ([bind_filter_eval], with the statement's arguments now threaded into the walk because a consumer's WHERE may carry `?`) and sends it down with the cap.
    **WHAT STILL BLOCKS, and it is the same list:** an ORDER BY or a window above the filter cancels the cap outright, because the engine runs the whole body under `FIRST 1 ... And a filter NOTHING passes must run the body out, five iterations, which is the cap simply never being reached; both are cells that pass on BOTH binaries, which is what makes them controls rather than passengers.

NULL: a slot typed by an expression that READS NO COLUMN is NOT NULL (`? = 1 + 1`, `? = CAST('x' AS CHAR(3))`, `? = UPPER('abc')`), while one over a column keeps that column's nullability (`? = I + 1` stays nullable) - exactly [expr_has_col], and the axis on which `? = 1.5` and `? = DATE '...'` differed by nothing else at all.

UNION ALL ...` to 1 - and that **a `WITH` statement is typed by its MAIN select**: a plain CTE is 12, `WITH C AS (...) SELECT DISTINCT ... FOR UPDATE` is 1, and a `DISTINCT` inside the CTE BODY leaves it at 12. Neither branch had ever been probed; the draft would have shipped a guess on both.
    **THE DISTINCT READER CAME FREE FROM THE PREVIOUS CHUNK, and it is the reason a leading-word test will not do.** `SELECT FIRST 2 DISTINCT ID ... FOR UPDATE` and `SELECT SKIP 1 DISTINCT ID ... FOR UPDATE` both cancel to 1, while `DISTINCT FIRST` is a syntax error - exactly the shapes [proj_distinct] was written for one chunk earlier, where the same keyword decided a `WITH LOCK` refusal. `COUNT(DISTINCT x)`, a `'DISTINCT'` LITERAL and `IS [NOT] DISTINCT FROM` are all still 12, and `FIRST`/`SKIP` alone are too.

Reading the info arm suggested the statement text was out of reach there, which pointed at a new per-handle map; `use_stmt!` then showed that [switch_stmt] already saves and restores `stmt_sql` in its `StmtSlot` ALONGSIDE the plan. So the text has exactly the plan's per-handle fidelity, and the fix is one bool derived from it at each emitter - no `Plan` variant, no walker touched, and nothing that can go stale between statements. [stmt_type_of] keeps its signature and its six unit tests; the promotion lives in [stmt_type_announced]. The FLAG word needs no promotion at all: measured, a `FOR UPDATE` select answers 3 exactly as a plain one does, and [stmt_flags_of] already counts 12 as a cursor type.

Into NUMERIC(9,2) with 1.115 bound: `? * 2` and `? * 2.0` store 2.00 (the value became 1), `2 * ?` stores 2.24, `? / 2` 0.56, `? + 0` and `? - 0` 1.12; into NUMERIC(9,4) `? * 2` bound 1.11115 is 2.0000; `? * ?`, `? * <column>`, `(? * 2) + 0` and `? * 2 * 2` follow the same left-operand rule, and a DOUBLE destination keeps its double (2.23). SQLDA_DISPLAY announces the destination's own scale in every one of them, so the slot PUBLISHED and the conversion APPLIED differ - which is why this is a value-path law, not a describe one.
    A DECFLOAT destination now converts through its slot too (`(DF) VALUES (? / 3)` bound 10 is 3.333333333333333333333333333333333, the decimal division), which retired the explicit DECFLOAT refusals on both the INSERT and UPDATE arms: a decfloat VALUE travels to the store as its exact decimal text, since `WireParam` has no decfloat carrier and the destination's encoder already reads one by the decNumber grammar (`serve-real-slottype`, 2026-09-16).
  - **A `?` INSIDE an IN / NOT IN / EXISTS / scalar SUBQUERY, answered instead of refused** - the last of the bind-error leftovers, and a MECHANISM change rather than a vector one. An uncorrelated subquery is evaluated AT PREPARE and folded to literal tokens, which a placeholder cannot survive; a parameter-bearing one now takes the PER-ROW route instead ([resolve_subqueries] declines the fold on `text_has_param`), where its `?` is rewritten to an `FC$PRM<slot>` marker - the same mechanism the outer references already use - and the bound value is spelled in as a SQL literal at bind ([subst_prm_markers] in `subst_params_expr`, with a fresh cache per bind). The slot NUMBERS in text order: `corr_register` takes the clause's base plus the placeholders written before the subquery plus the slots earlier subqueries claimed, the inner DESCRIPTORS come from the inner plan's own input sink (published through `CORR_PRM` so the statement's describe announces them), and the outer parser skips those slots when it meets the subquery's token - so `WHERE I = ? AND ID IN (SELECT .. WHERE I = ?)` binds outer-then-inner and the reverse spelling binds inner-then-outer. The raise waits for the inner stream exactly as the engine's does: an empty inner side answers, and so does an empty OUTER one (`serve-real-bindconv`, 2026-09-16).

- **NOT DONE, BY DESIGN - collation-aware DISTINCT / GROUP BY / UNION over a case/accent-insensitive collation:** the engine answers these; fire-crab refuses (`coll_groupable_ttype`, server.rs:45469, deliberately rejects ICU Secondary/Primary). Researched and left as-is: the comparison side already works (ORDER BY and `=` under a CI collation are correct), but a collapsed CI group has NO specified survivor spelling - the engine returns different members for `DISTINCT` vs `GROUP BY` vs `GROUP BY ... MIN(x)` over the same rows (measured). Producing a survivor would be a guess at an unspecified value, which the refuse-rather-than-guess law forbids; the refusal is correct. (`COUNT`/cardinality would be right, but the projected key spelling would be a coin toss.)

Wrong answers first; a refusal is law-safe and ranks below any wrong answer.

- **Parameter slot typing inside an expression: DONE** (`serve-real-slottype`, 2026-09-16) - see the entry in the answered list.

- **An exponent literal stored into a DECFLOAT column keeps its TEXT** (1E+200 stays 1E+200, 1.5E-398 stores 2E-398); refused today - needs the literal spelling carried to the store encoder.
- **DECFLOAT leftovers** (exponent overflow / underflow, out-of-range literals, text clamping and SUM over opposite infinities are DONE - `serve-real-dfoverflow`, `serve-real-dfliteral`): an out-of-range text stored into a DECFLOAT column refuses where the engine raises the overflow vector; `UPDATE .. SET <decfloat> = <out-of-DOUBLE-range literal>` refuses where the engine stores it.
- **The engine's decimal-to-DOUBLE literal conversion is imprecise near DOUBLE's lower limit** (`1e-307` renders 1.000000000000000e-307, `1.5e-308` renders 0 while `1e-308` does not); fire-crab's correctly rounded parse differs (DOUBLE on both, render-only, low).
- **Bind-error leftovers** (a plain column, an expression left side, the wide magnitudes, `CAST(? AS <type>)`, a JOIN's ON and a SUBQUERY's own `?` are all DONE - `serve-real-bindconv`): what still refuses with the generic *Dynamic SQL Error*. A subquery `?` reached through a caller that cannot say where the statement's numbering starts - the DML WHERE paths and the view-body resolver pass `param_base: None` to [resolve_subqueries], which keeps the old refusal rather than take a slot number it cannot prove (binding the wrong value to it would be a silent wrong answer); only the single-table SELECT path proves its base today. A **TEXT cast target** (`S = CAST(? AS VARCHAR(5))`, refused for a FITTING value too): the slot's charset is the ATTACHMENT's, which [cast_target_descriptor] leaves flat, while the projection resolver types the cast source UTF8 - and [cmp_sides]' text path reconciles byte-carrier against real charsets, so admitting it would GUESS a charset for a NONE column. The engine raises *string right truncation, expected length 5, actual 10* for an over-long value, and the projection `SELECT CAST(? AS VARCHAR(5))` already answers it - only the comparison side is left. Also still refusing: a text whose exponent underflows (`I < ?` ['1e-400'], where the engine compares against a tiny positive - a zero column value sorts BELOW it, so sign alone cannot decide it), and capital-hex '0X10' (the engine reads uninitialized memory). Law-safe, vector and timing differ.
- **Refusals of common constructs** (law-safe): number-beside-text UNION (VARYING typing), a DECFLOAT literal in `=`/IN outside the param path, DECFLOAT builtins (COMPARE_DECFLOAT, NORMALIZE_DECFLOAT, QUANTIZE, TOTALORDER), SET DECFLOAT ROUND / TRAPS, a conforming driver binding blr_dec64 / blr_dec128 raw, multi-column UNION, HAVING over a decfloat aggregate, a decfloat IN-subquery, `WHERE CURRENT OF`, GROUP BY / window + FIRST/SKIP/ROWS, collation-aware DISTINCT (by design, below).

### Third-hunt top find - DONE for CAST + equality/ordering (see the DONE entry above); the pattern/blob/none-column/col-vs-col tails remain

- **A NONE-charset text value compared to (or cast at) a REAL charset is a SILENT WRONG ANSWER - the highest-severity find of the third hunt, and BIGGER than the hunt agent's "one-spot blob fix" claim (verified by direct measurement).** Under the default isql attachment, which is effectively NONE (`CHAR_LENGTH('café')` is 5 on both servers), the engine treats a NONE operand's BYTES as already being in the other side's charset: `WHERE v = 'café'` over a UTF8 column MATCHES (the NONE literal's `c3 a9` bytes read as UTF8 `café`), and `CAST(<utf8 text blob> AS VARCHAR(n))` - which describes as charset NONE on BOTH servers - carries the blob's RAW STORED BYTES (`octet_length` 5), untransliterated. fire-crab instead carrier-decodes the NONE bytes into carrier chars and re-encodes/compares them as real codepoints, so the SAME equality returns 0 (a qualifying row silently vanishes), `POSITION('é' IN b)` is 0, and the NONE cast decodes-then-`carrier_encode`s to 4 bytes (`café` -> `63 61 66 e9`). The `octet_length`/`char_length` of the blob and of an EXPLICIT-charset cast are already right; only the NONE-context byte identity and the NONE-vs-real comparison are wrong. The correct model is the engine's: **a byte-carrier (NONE/OCTETS) operand is bytes - a comparison against a real charset compares the real side's ENCODED bytes to the carrier's bytes, and a blob-to-NONE cast passes the stored bytes through.** **RE-MEASURED 2026-09-17 AND MOSTLY CLOSED - read this before planning from the paragraph above.** The EQUALITY half and the blob-to-NONE CAST half both AGREE now (`WHERE u = 'café'` matches a UTF8 column and `CAST(<utf8 blob> AS VARCHAR(n))` is 5 octets on both servers), closed by `f692502`'s byte-space reinterpretation; LIKE - both the match and the engine's 22000 raise - is closed by the entry above. What REMAINS, measured cell by cell: `POSITION`, `REPLACE` and `TRIM` with a non-ASCII needle and `CONTAINING` over a BLOB, which sit on the SysFn/blob paths rather than the predicate builders (`POSITION('é' IN u)` engine 4 / fc 0, `REPLACE` 4 / 5, `TRIM(TRAILING 'é')` 3 / 5, and the MIRROR direction under a UTF8 attachment where the NONE column is the carrier); and a BOUND LIKE pattern, unreachable at bind because `Predicate::bind` takes no descriptors. Its framing was ALSO wrong twice - see "Stale claims retired": the fix did not touch `coll_value_cmp`, and the raise does not turn on the column's byte width. Measured 2026-09-08; re-measured and narrowed 2026-09-17, and narrowed AGAIN the same day - the LITERAL side of the function family closed with the string-function entry above, so what is left here is exactly TWO shapes, both needing the VALUES reconciled in byte space at EVAL rather than a literal rewritten at prepare. (1) THE MIRROR - a carrier COLUMN meeting a REAL literal under a real attachment: `POSITION('é' IN N)` 4/0, `POSITION(N IN 'xcafé')` 2/0, `REPLACE(N,'é','e')` 4/7, `TRIM(TRAILING 'é' FROM N)` 3/5, `N CONTAINING 'é'` 1/0, while `N LIKE '%é%'` agrees (observed, unexplained). (2) COLUMN-vs-COLUMN, where there is no literal to rewrite at all: `POSITION(N IN V)` and `POSITION(V IN N)` 1/0, `TRIM(TRAILING N FROM V)` 0/5, `REPLACE(V,N,'x')` 1/5 under BOTH attachments, plus three shapes fire-crab REFUSES rather than answering wrongly - `V CONTAINING N`, `N CONTAINING V`, `V LIKE N`. **BOTH SHAPES RESOLVED 2026-09-18 as far as the FUNCTION path reaches.** Shape (2)'s four wrong answers are FIXED, and shape (1)'s are fixed for `POSITION`/`REPLACE`/`TRIM`; the fix is operand-keyed ([carrier_fn_operands]) rather than a literal rewritten at prepare, which is exactly what this entry predicted was needed and is why it reaches column-vs-column at all. The three REFUSALS turned out NOT to belong to this family: measured, fire-crab refuses a non-literal LIKE/CONTAINING pattern even when both sides carry the SAME charset (`U CONTAINING V`, `U LIKE V`, and an expression pattern `U CONTAINING V||''`), so they are a missing capability, recorded as `refuses` cells. `CONTAINING` over a carrier with a LITERAL needle remains divergent on purpose - it is the predicate path, not the function path. **CLOSED 2026-09-18 as well, in its own slice** (`serve-real-nonecmp` 96, 2 flip on `302c4d1`): both of CONTAINING's arms - the expression arm and the plain-COLUMN fast path - now take the symmetric condition, while the shared literal path they sit beside is untouched. **So shape (1) of this entry is fully closed and shape (2)'s wrong answers were closed by the slice before it**; what remains from this paragraph is only the non-literal-pattern capability gap, which measurement moved out of this family entirely.


- **A SELECT OF AN UNALIASED NON-ASCII STRING LITERAL NO LONGER DROPS THE CONNECTION DONE (2026-09-08, `serve-real-litname`):** `SELECT '<non-ascii>' FROM RDB$DATABASE` with no column alias PANICKED and dropped the connection (SQLSTATE 08006). The implicit-column-name derivation split a select item on the LAST whitespace to spot a trailing alias, matching UNICODE whitespace and then advancing ONE BYTE past it; a multibyte literal under a NONE attachment reads its UTF-8 high bytes one char per byte, so a `0xA0` byte decoded to U+00A0 NBSP (a two-byte whitespace char) and the one-byte advance landed inside it -> `char boundary` panic. Restricted the split to ASCII whitespace (SQL separates `expr alias` on real whitespace, and the one-byte advance is then always valid). The column is named `CONSTANT` and the value returned, as the engine does. Found by a second eight-surface differential hunt; it was the only HIGH (a crash) among that hunt's finds.
